text: The claim and the sale terms of rwb-partner, the case state of rwb-case, the right of rwb-access and the package and claim-window parameter of rwb-decision are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-partner owns partner and partner_user, only rwb-case writes recovery_case and assignment, only rwb-access answers a capability area and a right, and only rwb-decision governs the rule rows and the parameters with their versions. No source publishes the four operation names, so none may be invented. The plan's C row for this slice is empty, so the five rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata.
read: FSD S6 A2.13.2 and A2.13.3.3; TSD S6 T5.2, T6.1 and T-A.1; context pack ownership rows and connection-matrix row S6; Template and Rules v1 R5.4 and R5.5 DP-11
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6009-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 11 and 12.2; RWB-S6-E6009-CON sections 3, 7 AC3 and AC4, 11 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision, before the contract is tagged
impact: Both stories build on Day 1 against five contract fakes with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and a statement on a partner, recovery_case, assignment or rule_row table fails the boundary test

text: This step declares no REST operation of its own: the claim is read on the rwb-partner contract and reaches the Workbench through the partner channel, the review sits behind the lot read API-S6-002 and the data room read API-S6-004 of its siblings, and the award path API-S6-003 belongs to RWB-S6-E6005-APP.
why: TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes five operations for S6 and none is a claim or a claim-decision operation, while the legacy story lists two endpoint rows that the target gives to two sibling stories. A put-back operation invented here would claim another story's surface and would put a business operation on the contract that no owner has baselined. The partner channel and its DMZ gateway have no story row in the plan, in the platform epics or in the X rows of this slice.
read: TSD S6 T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD S6 A2.13.2 (integration points Partner portal, ALS and GL); context pack Architecture v5 slide 8 notes (partner gateway in front of rwb-partner); legacy RWB-E6-009 Endpoints

confirm: Solution architect and the owners of the edge stories and of rwb-partner, before the contract is tagged
impact: The app story is reached through two sibling surfaces and the partner channel, and a story that declares the award path or the data room read as its own fails the review

text: The claim window of R-DS-34 and R-DS-39 is a versioned parameter read with its version and never a length in code; its value, its parameter name and its contract operation are Not specified in the source documents and are carried as placeholders, with the default ruling's parameter owner named as rwb-case (P3).
why: R-DS-34 fires on CLAIM_WINDOW_CLOSED with the timer 'per claim window', and neither the Business Rules workbook, the FSD nor the TSD gives the window a length or a parameter row, and no column carries it. Writing a number would be a business value invented by the builder. DP-06 is not in the pattern set of this key, so its H and C rows are recorded rather than added to the metadata.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-34, R-DS-35 and R-DS-39; FSD S6 A2.13.3.1; TSD S6 T4; Template and Rules v1 R3 (default ruling: parameters and reference data, P3 rwb-case) and R5.5 DP-06
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6009-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 5 X7, 8 BR6, 12.2, 13 and 19; RWB-S6-E6009-CON sections 3, 7 AC4, 8 BR8, 11, 12.2 and 19
confirm: Business lead, solution architect and the parameter owner in rwb-case, before the package is tagged
impact: The window is resolved at run time with its version recorded with each outcome, and no length appears in the build, the tests or the examples

text: The realized recovery by lot and by buyer of R-DS-34 and R-DS-39 is held on the existing account selling_price and the closed lot and served as a derived element on the lot read; no column is added, no event is published, and rwb-reporting is named as the eventual consumer with no contract or event allocated yet.
why: Neither debt_sale_lot nor debt_sale_account carries a realized-recovery column and the service's contracted event set holds only EV-23 LotAwarded, while the rule row names the monolith's Recovery Data Store and Power BI, which DP-17 removes with the data lake. Inventing a column or a new event would change the schema and the contract without an owner, so the value is derived from data that exists and the reporting path is recorded.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-34 and R-DS-39; TSD S6 T3.1; FSD S6 A2.13.3.1; Event and Messaging Design v4 row EV-23; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17 and R5.6

confirm: Solution architect, the data steward and the reporting owner, before the reporting contract or event is allocated
impact: The figure is computed from the closed lot's account set, no migration is added, no event is published, and the reporting gap is tracked rather than filled by the builder

text: The four legacy criteria stay owned by RWB-S6-E6009-APP word for word while the behaviour they name is partly a sibling story's: R-DS-29's transfer is RWB-S6-E6007-APP's, the GL_POSTED state and the reversal of R-DS-37 are RWB-S6-E6008-APP's, and the settlement adjustment of R-DS-36 is rwb-payment's and the settlement story's; those parts are faked here.
why: The plan assigns AC1 to AC4 of RWB-E6-009 to this key, and Template and Rules R7 forbids rewording or dropping a legacy criterion, yet FEAT-DBS-13 depends on FEAT-DBS-11 and the criteria name the transfer and the posting states that two sibling features create. Splitting the criteria would break the ownership rule and executing the siblings' rules here would duplicate them, so the criteria are kept and the sibling activity is faked.

impact: The criteria are proved on the fakes and against the published contracts of the two sibling stories in SIT; a claim is raised only after the transferred and posted states are reached

text: The case move is answered and never written: rwb-case owns recovery_case, assignment and every route state, and where it publishes a REST case-move operation its name is Not specified in the source documents; on the workflow boundary the answer is the stage outcome the parent CaseWorkflow applies.
why: No source publishes a REST operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage, and the connection-matrix row for S6 names Temporal to P7 with no REST call to P3. A story that wrote a case row would break the ownership rule and the one-writer principle, so the move is described as a boundary element.
